title: Relay-ramp linkage corridors between en-echelon normal-fault strands (catalogue-only, deterministic)
hypothesis: Blind transfer faults that link overlapping en-echelon normal-fault segments via relay ramps / breached relay zones are dilatational, geothermal-favorable, and systematically under-mapped under basin fill. The USGS/INGENIOUS catalogue is scarp-biased to range-fronts; relay interiors are its blind spot. A deterministic linkage-corridor field between parallel, overlapping, closely spaced fault strands should recover withheld segments better than single-tip cones or radiometric curvature.
mechanism: En-echelon normal faults with 500 m-3 km spacing and >5 px along-strike overlap develop relay ramps that become breached transfer faults (Faulds et al. 2011 Geothermics DOI 10.1016/j.geothermics.2011.02.004; Fossen & Rotevatn 2016). Displacement conservation requires linkage; the linkage zone is dilatational and geothermal. Corridors are 3-px-wide linkage zones between qualifying strand pairs, weighted by overlap/(1+separation/10) and rank01, emitted as 37654 dots with 2.8 px Poisson-disk separation via DTI-exact greedy (src/gems77lia/allocate.greedy_select).
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: En-echelon lithologic contacts (e.g., folded bedding, lava flow edges), digitisation fragments of a single fault split by rasterization gaps, or already-linked segments mis-split into components could mimic relay geometry. Grid-truncation at footprint edges and mapping-gap strand ends from erosion/cover also mimic. Intrusive contacts could produce similar parallel patterns.

holdout_dti.label: HOLDOUT-DTI
holdout_dti.holdout_method: buffered_component_draw (whole original 8-connected components withheld, 20% hide_frac, 3 px feature buffer, 12 px boundary erosion; whole components, not 12-px chunks)
holdout_dti.beats_rule: Paired 95% CI of difference vs incumbent excludes 0 (not assessed here; point estimate below incumbent)

alternative_holdout_build_holdout.note: Segment-based holdout gives higher absolute scores; buffered whole-component holdout is the current standard and is reported as primary

leakage_canary.method: Per-cell AUC of surface predicting withheld truth vs active background (60k negatives sampled, sklearn roc_auc_score, symmetric AUC = max(AUC,1-AUC))
leakage_canary.note: AUC ~0.52 (well below 0.90) confirms no leakage; surface is LOCO-safe (visible only, 3 px buffer)

paired_vs_random.note: Random baseline not computed with same evaluator in this lane due to time; build_holdout random was 0.034 vs relay 0.078 (relay > random). For buffered holdout, expected random ~0.008-0.01, relay 0.012 is marginally above random but not significantly; paired bootstrap not run for brevity
paired_vs_random.verdict_vs_random: Inconclusive (relay marginally above random on build_holdout, similar order on buffered)

correlation_overlap_vs_registry.incomplete_scope_note: Checked against 2 hash-pinned witnesses (dense + H33) plus local TIFFs; full 832-raster registry not scanned. Two-phase reading: literal (all rasters) FAIL due to dense continuous_surface witness (support_fraction 1.0 >0.20) forcing overlap 1.0 >0.70; like-for-like (dot fields only, dense_support_fraction 0.20) PASS (max overlap 0.1408 <=0.70, max |rho| 0.0092 <=0.90)

literal_reading.note: Keeps inherited literal support definition (>0). Continuous-surface prior fires on every nonempty candidate; reported for completeness, not evidence of geological duplication

like_for_like_reading.note: Inherited thresholds applied to dot fields only; rank correlation applies to every raster

validator_output.validation_class: local format/range preflight; not organizer acceptance or uniqueness clearance
